page: Microsoft Azure B32as_v2 is a general-purpose, burstable virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at up to 3.525 GHz. Based on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 32 vCPUs distributed across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The configuration is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance operates without integrated local storage or dedicated hardware GPUs, relying on remote network-attached disks for persistence.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, placing in the top quartile for stress-ng single-threaded execution, while multi-core throughput and PassMark CPU scores sit within the middle tiers. Memory subsystem testing reflects strong performance under PassMark memory benchmarks, supported by an uncached read bandwidth of 91.22 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth of 49.75 GB/sec. Workloads executing small-model LLM text generation also demonstrate strong throughput, whereas large 70B parameter prompt processing falls into the lower 25% bracket due to CPU-bound execution limitations and absence of vector acceleration extensions like AVX-512 or AMX.

The burstable CPU model allows organizations to acquire significant core counts and memory capacity with high cost efficiency when workloads exhibit variable or intermittent processing demands. The primary architectural tradeoff is the burstable resource credit dynamic, making sustained heavy compute inefficient compared to non-burstable tiers. Microsoft Azure B32as_v2 is well-matched for variable traffic web serving, software build servers, staging environments, batch data processing, and intermittent business application workloads.

The instance does not feature local storage or GPU accelerators, depending entirely on remote storage volumes for system and data persistence. Benchmarks highlight strong single-core CPU and memory throughput, while multi-core metrics and decompression speeds remain in the median tier. Due to its burstable resource profile, the server delivers high cost efficiency for fluctuating compute demands rather than uninterrupted full-capacity execution. Microsoft Azure B32as_v2 is suitable for intermittent enterprise applications, moderate database operations, code compilation pipelines, and variable-load web serving.
